messages:
Maya: heads-up — our spot GPU spend spiked 18% in eu-west last week because a bunch of inference pools got preempted and we melted into on-demand. need a better transparent fallback plan so apps don't overprovision
Carl: did we confirm it was simultaneous preempts or cascading scale-ups from the autoscaler?
Maya: InfraBot shows a cluster-wide termination wave at 2109875020 in eu-west-1 — multiple node groups of p4->p3p. autoscaler reacted, bumped nodegroups, then workloads shifted to higher-cost instances
Lekha: autoscaler config: we have scale-up cooldown 0s, scale-down-delay 10m. scale-up being instant is fine but scale-down is too slow for churn — but faster scale-down will risk thrash
Jorge: suggestion: add a short-lived warm pool with tainted nodes for opportunistic GPU capacity (keeps KV cache ephemeral) and only let critical pods tolerate the taint. when preemptions happen, fallback to a reserve group with pre-warmed images
Priya: watch out for cross-region fallback. last incident we routed traffic to ap-southeast and egress costs ballooned. we should prefer local fallbacks and only cross-region for <1% of traffic
Carl: We can implement a scoring function for fallback targets: score = (latency_penalty * latency_norm) + (cost_penalty * cost_norm) + (egress_penalty * egress_estimate). pick lowest score under capacity constraints
Lekha: implementation details for k8s: mixed nodegroup annotation + taints. example taint we use: "optimistic=true:NoSchedule" and pods that can fall back include toleration with tolerationSeconds=300 to allow graceful eviction
Maya: lifecycle hook idea: preStop on node drains runs a lightweight shim to flush in-memory KV to S3/redis replica. small script attached in thread:
Maya: ```
# /opt/node-drain-hooks/flush-cache.sh
kubectl exec -n infra cache-pod -- /app/flush --target=s3://redwood-evict-cache/${NODE_NAME}
```
Jorge: also add an admission webhook to mark pods that are true-critical (priorityClassName=system-cluster-critical) so they get bumped to reserved on-demand pool instead of shared spot fallback
Priya: operational policy: if fallback causes >$X/day extra egress or >Y% latency degradation, trigger an automated rollback to pinned model variant (smaller model) rather than cross-region route
Carl: autoscaler knobs: consider expander: "least-waste" + mixed-instance-policy on nodegroup to prefer smaller cheaper GPUs first. also set scaleDownUtilizationThreshold so we don't keep >10% spare capacity after a burst
Lekha: small k8s snippet for toleration with seconds:
Lekha: ```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "optimistic"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
    tolerationSeconds: 300
```
InfraBot: incident summary posted to #incidents: 2109875020 preemption wave. affected clusters: eu-west-1-prod, eu-west-1-stage. estimated extra cost: $3.1k
Maya: action items: 1) Carl to prototype fallback scoring function (deadline Wed EOD) 2) Lekha to repo PR for warm pool + tolerations + preStop hook (Thu) 3) Jorge to prototype admission webhook for critical pods (Fri) 4) Priya to add egress caps and alerting on cost/latency (Mon)
Carl: I'll put a simple PoC that uses prometheus + price API & latency probe. will post link to PR
Jorge: I'll make the webhook idempotent and add unit tests for label-based exemptions
Priya: will add a synthetic test to catch cross-region egress spikes and a pager threshold
Maya: thanks team. prioritize tests — we want predictable economics before Q2 customer ramp :thumbsup:
Lekha: +1
InfraBot: scheduled a runbook rehearsal for the fallback plan on 2109878000 (TZ: UTC). Invite sent to oncall and infra-engineers
Maya: closing the thread — will follow up on PRs in #eng-infra-updates
